newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy police nab $59 million from alleged Mafiosi.
newsitem.headline: Italy police nab $59 million from alleged Mafiosi.

text.p: Italian police said on Saturday they had seized some 100 billion lire ($59 million) in assets belonging to businessmen with alleged ties to the 'Ndrangheta, the Calabrian Mafia.

The assets included seven companies, real estate, a Ferrari "Testa Rossa" sports car and bank accounts, police said. Among the companies involved were a petroleum products dealer and makers of aerosol sprays and containers.
Police identified the owners of the assets as Giovanni, Vincenzo and Paolo Ruggiero of the nearby town of Gioia Tauro.
They are suspected of links with the Piromalli clan of the local Mafia, known as the 'Ndrangheta.
Italian authorities have recently dealt heavy blows to businessmen they suspect of Mafia ties.
Last month, Palermo police said they had confiscated assets worth more than one trillion lire from a jailed Sicilian construction company owner, Vincenzo Piazza.
Piazza, who has been in prison for three years on charges of links with the Mafia, officially declared a gross monthly income of 1.8 million lire ($1,000) in 1989.
